Article Title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI and sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution that lays down the anti-defection framework.Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985.In a post on X, TMC Lok Sabha MP Mahua Moitra shared the photo of one of the notices issued to rebel MPs and said, “Cover up caught out!” Highlighting that TMC had filed 20 disqualification petitions in June, Moitra said, “Speaker LS did nothing except give them better seats at our expense. SG Tushar Mehta in Court said the Speaker had issued notices. Notice dated Aug 25th -- exact date of hearing!”On Tuesday, Supreme Court sought a response from Lok Sabha Speaker’s office on time-bound adjudication of TMC’s petition seeking disqualification of rebel MPs who broke away from the party after its electoral debacle in West Bengal, even as Abhishek Banerjee accused Speaker Om Birla of “deliberate inaction”.The SC also issued notices to the 20 rebel MPs: Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachna Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Abu Teher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Kalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.In his petition, Abhishek Banerjee told the court on Tuesday that he had lodged the disqualification petition against the rebel MPs on June 18 and complained that despite the lapse of two months, no meaningful progress has been made on its adjudication.The continuing delay in the adjudication process is impacting democratic governance, he said.In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June. Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on the pending petitions.
Article Summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who have aligned with NCPI. The notices sought their responses within seven days on petitions filed by TMC national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee seeking their disqualification.

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday waded into Bihar’s escalating BPSC row, questioning the Samrat Choudhary-led government over allegations of exam irregularities and paper leaks. He referred to the police crackdown on protesting students, saying, “questions don't stop with batons.”His statement came a day after a clash broke out between students and police in Bihar's capital, with police using water cannons and barricades to stop the protesters from marching.Rahul described it as a “straightforward” question on behalf of Bihar’s students and posted on X: “Why the irregularities in recruitment exams? Why no action on allegations of paper leaks? And how long will this tampering with the future of the youth continue?”He then targeted the long-standing BJP-JD(U)-led government in Bihar, saying, “The controversy over BPSC exams is not of today. Students have been on the streets for a long time over the recruitment process, exam pattern, delays, and transparency.”The Lok Sabha leader of opposition also referred to the use of an AK-47 by a security personnel during an earlier student protest in Bihar, which coincided with student protests in Delhi and across the country over NEET fiasco.“But instead of answering, what is the government doing? It's wielding batons and water cannons.It's taking students into custody. In Siwan, there was even firing with an AK 47 on protesters,” the former Congress chief said.He added in his post: “This is not just a question of police action. This is a question of the mindset of that BJP government, which has no answers - and that's why it's turning the police into a weapon to evade accountability.”“The BJP government should understand this - questions don't stop with batons. You can't snatch away someone's future by instilling fear,” the Rae Bareli added.Bihar students had marched towards Raj Bhavan and chief minister Samrat Choudhary's residence to stage a “gherao”, but faced police barricading and some of them were detained in Patna.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi questions Samrat Choudhary-led government over allegations of exam irregularities and paper leaks. His statement came a day after a clash broke out between students and police in Bihar's capital, with police using water cannons and barricades.

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who are now affiliated with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), seeking their responses within seven days to disqualification petitions filed by the TMC.The disqualification petitions are currently pending before Birla.This comes after Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta on Tuesday informed the Supreme Court that the Speaker had already issued notices to the 20 MPs on the disqualification petitions filed by the TMC under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.Mehta made the submission before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant while appearing for the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House. The bench was hearing a plea filed by senior TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, challenging the delay in deciding the petitions seeking the disqualification of the rebels.Responding to the submission, the bench said, "It is not a question of issuing notices, it is a question of concluding the proceedings within a time frame."During the hearing, the bench indicated that it was inclined to issue notices to the respondents on Abhishek Banerjee’s writ petition.Mehta, however, submitted that there was no need to issue notices to the Speaker or his office, stating that he would appear on behalf of Birla.The TMC has accused the 20 MPs of “abandoning” the party and subsequently joining the NCPI. Abhishek Banerjee has contended that their conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.The petition names the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House as the principal respondents and also impleads the MPs whose disqualification is being sought.The respondents are Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs. The MPs are now affiliated with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) The disqualification petitions are currently pending before the Speaker.

Dad accused of sexually abusing girl

Nagpur:





A case has been registered under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against a man for allegedly sexually abusing and exploiting his 14-year-old daughter over the past year. The man also allegedly threatened to kill the girl and her mother.As per the complaint lodged at Sadar police station, the sexual exploitation had been happening since early January 2025. Officials said a thorough probe will be conducted to ensure justice for the survivor.

Article Title: File culpable homicide case in Amravati fire, says oppn
Article Text:
Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar addresses the media

Nagpur:





Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sushma Andhare on Wednesday demanded strict action over the deaths of three newborns in the fire at District Women’s Hospital in Amravati, alleging serious safety lapses.Wadettiwar demanded that responsibility be fixed within eight days and those guilty be charged with culpable homicide. He also sought Rs 25 lakh compensation for each bereaved family and Rs 5 lakh for contractual staff who helped rescue newborns.Wadettiwar alleged that permanent posts in govt hospitals remained vacant, forcing dependence on contractual staff. He also questioned the quality of ventilators supplied to the hospital and demanded replacement of around 10,000 such machines installed across the state. He alleged fire and electrical safety audits had also expired.Andhare alleged that the fire audit had not been conducted despite reminders from the Civil Surgeon. She questioned the role of PWD officials and demanded culpable homicide charges against those responsible.Andhare also targeted guardian minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule for not visiting the hospital and alleged that govt had failed to provide Rs 9.5 crore for basic facilities while sanctioning Rs 121 crore for the Hanuman Gadhi project.She demanded that the inquiry committee include the District Civil Surgeon and PWD engineers. She warned of an agitation if action was not taken within seven days.
Article Summary: Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sushma Andhare on Wednesday demanded strict action over the deaths of three newborns in the fire at District Women’s Hospital in Amravati.

Article Title: 189 soyabean seed samples in Amravati found sub-standard
Article Text:
Amravati





: Out of 464 samples of soyabean seeds taken for analysis from the district, 189 have been found to be sub-standard in reports received till till August 17 . Action is being taken against the seed producing company in this regard, said district superintending agriculture officer Rahul Satpute.After farmers complained that soyabean seeds failed to germinate, agriculture department issued orders to the seed producing companies to submit distributor-wise, variety-wise and lot-wise information of supplies in the district. Taluka-level grievance redressal committees have been constituted to ensure inspection of complaints.Criminal cases have been registered in the district against the seed producing companies. Out of the 3,157 complaints received regarding soybean seeds, 2,326 are against a particular company against which a criminal case has been registered at Gadgenagar police station in Amravati.
Article Summary: Out of 464 samples of soyabean seeds taken for analysis from the district, 189 have been found to be sub-standard. Action is being taken against the seed producing company in this regard. Out of the 3,157 complaints received regarding soybean seeds, 2,326 are against a particular company.

Article Title: Samruddhi’s Igatpuri tunnel to be shut for an hour on Aug 27
Article Text:
Nashik:





A section of the Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi expressway will remain closed for an hour on Thursday afternoon for safety testing inside the Igatpuri tunnel.According to highway police, the tunnel lane carrying traffic from Nagpur towards Mumbai will be shut from noon to 1 pm for controlled fire and performance testing of the modular fire suppression demo unit installed inside the tunnel.Motorists travelling on the expressway will be diverted via the Mumbai-Agra highway from Pimpri Sado during the closure.Highway police superintendent Nilesh Sonawane has directed highway police units, MSRDC and local police to coordinate traffic management and ensure smooth diversions during the exercise.
Article Summary: A section of the Nagpur-Mumbai Samruddhi expressway will remain closed for an hour on Thursday afternoon for safety testing inside the Igatpuri tunnel. The tunnel lane carrying traffic from Nagpur towards Mumbai will be shut from noon to 1 pm for controlled fire and performance testing.

Article Title: Monsoon preparedness: TN assigns ministers, officers to monitor Chennai
Article Text:
A woman walking with an umbrella to shield herself from the rain on Wednesday evening in Chennai

Chennai:





Tamil Nadu govt has named eight ministers and senior IAS officers to monitor development works, flood preparedness and disaster management across Chennai’s 15 zones.Highways minister Aadhav Arjuna will oversee the entire Chennai, while minister Ramesh will be in charge of Thiruvottiyur and Manali; Lokesh of Madhavaram and Tondiarpet; Arunraj of Royapuram and Thiru Vi Ka Nagar; Vijay Balaji of Ambattur, Anna Nagar and Teynampet; TK Prabhu of Kodambakkam and Valasaravakkam; Vijay Parthiban of Alandur and Adyar; and K Vignesh of Perungudi and Sholinganallur.Separately, one senior IAS officer has been assigned to each GCC zone. The officers will coordinate with the GCC commissioner and monitor vulnerable areas, relief material and personnel deployment, sanitation, traffic and logistics, medical assistance and emergency shelters.The ministers and the officials will inspect flood hotspots, stuck civic projects and coordinate with officials to expedite them.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu govt has named eight ministers and senior IAS officers to monitor development works, flood preparedness and disaster management across Chennai’s 15 zones. The officers will coordinate with the GCC commissioner and monitor vulnerable areas, relief material and personnel deployment, sanitation, traffic and logistics.

Article Title: Lady doctor arrested near Salem for illegal fetal gender determination
Article Text: SALEM: Police on Wednesday arrested a lady doctor in Vazhapadi in Salem district on charges of illegally determining and disclosing the gender of fetuses to pregnant women. Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running in the area. They sealed the clinic.Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child.Acting on a complaint, a team led by joint director Dr S P Nandhini, Attur district health officer Dr N Yoganand and Vazhapadi Government Hospital chief medical officer Dr Ramesh Kumar raided the facility.They found that Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had received Rs 30,000 from a pregnant woman to determine the gender of her fetus. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.Health department officials said this was not the first violation by the clinic. It had been raided twice earlier, and Dr Selvamba Rajkumar had faced restrictions on conducting scans and treatments, they said. Cases were registered against her then too.
Article Summary: Health department officials seized scan equipment, abortion pills and cash from a clinic the doctor, Selvamba Rajkumar, was running. Authorities said the clinic on the Cuddalore Road charged pregnant women additional fees to reveal the gender of the unborn child. Dr Nandini said the doctor had been handed over to police for legal proceedings.

Article Title: DYFI, YC protest Railway Board’s decision to reorganize Palakkad railway division
Article Text:

DYFI has intensified its agitation against the Railway Board’s decision to reorganize Palakkad railway division, with protests being held at major railway stations across all districts of north Kerala.DYFI activists took out marches to major railway stations in Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Kannur and Kasaragod districts as part of the protest. Article Title: Two get five years’ imprisonment for attempting to murder homemaker
Article Text:
Idukki

:





The Idukki third additional district and sessions court has sentenced two men to five years’ imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 40,000 each for trespassing into a house and attempting to murder a woman by assaulting her. The verdict was delivered 13 years after the incident.Judge S S Seena convicted Shais, 44, of Ozhukkayil House at Mankuva in Konnathady, and Jayesh alias Chanthu, 38, of Plachery House at Munitandu in Mannamkandam, Adimali.The incident took place at a house in Pipeline area of Vellathooval village under Kunchithanny around 2am on April 24, 2013. According to the prosecution, the accused trespassed into the house and attacked the woman, a homemaker, while she was asleep in bed. The assault was allegedly carried out with the intention of killing her.Adimali police registered a case and launched an investigation. The probe was led by the then Adimali Inspector K Jinadevan. A chargesheet was subsequently filed against the accused.After considering the evidence and witness statements produced by the prosecution during the trial, the court found both accused guilty and sentenced them to jail.
Article Summary: Shais, 44, of Ozhukkayil House at Mankuva in Konnathady, and Jayesh alias Chanthu, 38, of Plachery House at Munitandu in Mannamkandam, Adimali, found guilty. The incident took place at a house in Pipeline area of Vellathooval village under Kunchithanny.
